title: Artificial Intelligence
overview: An interdisciplinary AI minor open to all majors, with a published 19-credit minimum. The detailed catalog inventory remains inaccessible.

sources.title: Minoring in Artificial Intelligence
sources.locator: Minoring in Artificial Intelligence; Artificial Intelligence program entry

outcomes.text: Combine machine learning, data analysis and responsible AI with attention to ethics, societal effects and interdisciplinary applications.

requirements.title: Minor credit minimum
requirements.summary: The department publishes this credit minimum; the detailed catalog course list is not accessible.

requirements.title: Open to all majors
requirements.summary: Students in any major may pursue the AI minor.

requirements.title: Minor declaration and certification
requirements.summary: Submit the completed minor form to the Registrar before the last add/drop day of the final semester. Student and department chair/program director signatures certify the listed courses.

requirements.title: Relationship to declared majors
requirements.summary: The minor must differ from the declared major. Students with two majors may not declare a minor. The AI overview permits all major fields; it does not remove these university-level conditions.

requirements.title: Minor grading
requirements.summary: Courses used for the minor cannot be taken Pass/Fail; the minor GPA must be at least 2.00.

requirements.title: Minor residency
requirements.summary: At least 9 credits toward the minor must be in residence unless the catalog specifies otherwise. AI-specific catalog exceptions remain unverified; the published amount is not normalized to a credit unit.

requirements.title: Minor substitutions and transfer exceptions
requirements.summary: For post-matriculation elective transfer credit (such as 1XX/2XX) or courses not listed as satisfying the minor, the form requires committee approval and an attached Major/Minor Substitution Waiver. The form names the Committee on Degrees; the linked advising site separately identifies its successor.

requirements.title: Academic exception committee context
requirements.summary: The advising site states that the Committee on Academic Exceptions replaces the former Committee on Degrees and Committee on Academic Status. It handles exception requests; no individual exception or AI-specific waiver is presumed. The minor declaration listing says no minor advisor is required.

notes: Curriculum evidence reviewed on 2026-10-10. The official catalog returned a JavaScript/robot challenge; no access restriction was bypassed. Department sources support the observations below, but a full catalog audit remains outstanding.
Published credits remain in source units (unknown normalized unit). Course credit values, descriptions, prerequisites, syllabi and calendar have not been inferred.

Public policy review 2026-10-11: Registrar declaration PDFs are also linked from current advising pages and departmental resources. Printed month-only revisions are retained in source locators; no day or effective catalog year is invented. The known catalog challenge was not retried. PDF text is manually reviewed evidence, not supported by the ordinary text-only HTTP scrape path.

The minor form still names the Committee on Degrees; current advising pages identify the Committee on Academic Exceptions as its successor. The general residency rule expressly permits catalog exceptions, which remain unverified for AI.
